# Review of Galaxy #23966

Reviewed `0216fb3c845dfd90e754f3fb03345dcc1177fe5b` against `dev` on 2026-10-11. Recommendation: **request changes**, for one reproduced P2. Draft remains unposted.

## Finding

**P2 — Encode generated Zarr keys when constructing HTTP request paths.**

Location: `lib/galaxy/files/uris.py:192`.

`rel_path` is a literal storage key obtained from Zarr metadata, but `fetch()` appends it directly to the directory URL. Valid array names such as `a b`, `a#b`, `a?b`, and `a%20b` therefore do not refer to the same remote object: spaces fail the HTTP file source's unencoded-character check, `#` becomes a fragment, `?` becomes a query, and `%20` is interpreted as an escape rather than a literal percent sequence. A consolidated store generated by Zarr can consequently fail materialization even though every required file exists.

The full `DatasetInstanceMaterializer.ensure_materialized()` reproducer produced dataset state `error` for all four names, and cleaned up each failed extra-files directory. An in-memory control that percent-encodes each generated HTTP key, preserving path separators and the already encoded root URL, produced state `ok` and values `[1, 2, 3]` in all four cases. No Galaxy files were changed. [Node-name rules](https://zarr-specs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/v3/core/index.html#node-names) permit these names, although the specification recommends a smaller portable character set.

Encode the key for HTTP/HTTPS sources at the URL-construction boundary, while retaining the literal relative path for the local destination and file sources that accept filesystem keys. Include spaces and a URL delimiter or literal percent escape in a round-trip regression.

## Design and coverage

The datatype hook leaves generic discovery/persistence in the materializer and Zarr enumeration in the datatype. Downloading via the selected file source keeps its access checks in use. The safe-relative-path check protects the local destination, worker exceptions are joined and propagated, temporary downloads are removed on failure, and persistence failure removes partial extra files from the object store. Existing tests exercise these behaviors substantively.

There are already clean integration building blocks: the threaded local HTTP server, reference-sized Zarr fixtures, `create_deferred_hda`, `DatasetPopulator`, and the `directory_listing` consumer. For the reported finding, reuse the existing job integration test with a legal encoded-name fixture and assert exact literal output paths; a reader/unit regression can cover encoded request paths. A consumer that reads array values is useful optional coverage: listing alone cannot prove chunk content correctness. An external bucket or distributed Galaxy deployment is unnecessary.

The body openly declares the large-store handler occupancy, missing-versus-denied 403 ambiguity on S3-style servers, and potentially incomplete listings from file sources that ignore recursion. These are real operating limitations rather than additional hidden findings. Treat listing completeness as a human acceptance decision: the materializer cannot certify a store copied from an incomplete listing.

Cross-PR context: #24005 adds directory normalization during fetch/discovered-output/metadata handling and removes `store_root`. This PR presently persists listed wrapper directories without a normalization hook. After combining them, test a deferred listable source containing a single wrapped Zarr store and decide where to call the new grooming hook before persistence and metadata. This is integration advice, not a standalone failure on the reviewed head.

## Risks

The download implementation is reversible, but the directory materialization contract and stricter handling of every failed deferred input establish behavior that tools and workflows will rely on.

<details><summary>Risk Details</summary>

- The new guard stops jobs for all failed deferred materializations, including non-directory inputs and hash mismatches; this extends beyond Zarr.
- Missing chunks are legitimate fill values, so discovery and status classification determine scientific correctness. On hosts returning 403 for missing objects, other denials can still become fill values, as the author documents.
- File sources that ignore recursion can produce incomplete copies that are accepted; the fsspec-limit check covers one specific truncation mechanism.
- Local job preparation occupies a handler thread during large downloads. Remote evaluation avoids that occupancy but requires the beta evaluation mode and extended metadata.
- Parallel file-source access assumes implementations and user-context lookups tolerate concurrent calls. The tests cover HTTP sessions and a simple listable source, not every authenticated backend.
- Metadata and chunk-key formats introduce a maintainable compatibility boundary; the reference probes cover ordinary v2/v3 and sharding, not every custom chunk-grid or storage-transformer extension.
- HTTP key encoding must preserve literal local names and avoid changing filesystem/file-source keys.

</details>

<details><summary>Risk Review Advice</summary>

Fix the reproduced encoding failure and add a case to the existing real-job test. Humans should explicitly accept the documented incomplete-listing and ambiguous-403 limits before using this for scientific production data, and confirm the desired policy change for non-directory failed deferred inputs.

When #24005 lands, verify wrapper normalization on a deferred directory through the combined materializer path. Consider a representative authenticated file source and a realistically sized store when deciding whether the documented local-handler cost is acceptable.

</details>
